original.target_description: Primary article verified: Housework Task Hierarchies in 32 Countries, Tai and Treas. Table 4 contains multilevel multinomial odds ratios for gender-typed, egalitarian, and pragmatic task performance, each relative to conforming, across numerous individual- and country-level predictors. The input supplies no study, description, or test locator to identify a coefficient or contrast.

replication.target_description: Unassigned side; not examined in this source-grouped completion.

notes: Only original n, effect size, and p were assigned. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Original target remains unidentified; no coefficient was selected from row order or numerical matching. Table 4, p. 788, reports odds ratios (metric explicitly established on p. 784), with three outcome contrasts relative to conforming. Candidate examples, in gender-typed / egalitarian / pragmatic column order: wife’s income higher 1.113 / 1.576*** / 1.127; liberal gender ideology 0.800** / 1.157*** / 1.003; husband’s work hours 1.011** / 0.998 / 1.004*; wife’s work hours 0.992* / 1.011*** / 1.005**; number of children 1.065 / 0.934* / 1.005; Southern European 3.112* / 0.469 / 0.704. Other predictors and controls in Table 4 are also possible targets. Printed two-tailed star bounds are * P < 0.05, ** P < 0.01, *** P < 0.001; no target-specific p was assigned. A coefficient without stars does not establish a printed exact p or a p lower bound. Common analytic sample candidate is 7,840 married men aged 18–65 in 32 countries, explicitly printed rather than calculated. It is retained in dispositions only for field-scope review because the row-specific target is unresolved. PDF pages 5 and 9 (printed pp. 784 and 788) were rendered and visually inspected; evidence quotes use canonical supplied text.
